findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on unreadable or missing file
findings.failure_mode: untrusted or missing file path aborts the entire program instead of returning a typed I/O or Parse error
findings.fix: Return a Result<Record, MetricError> with an I/O variant; use ? or map_err to propagate fs::read_to_string errors

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric or out-of-range field
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV line aborts the entire load_metrics call instead of returning a typed Parse error for that record
findings.fix: Return Result<Record, MetricError> with a Parse variant; use .parse::<u32>().map_err(|_| ParseError)? instead of unwrap()

findings.problem: as u16 lossy cast from parsed u32: any value > 65535 silently truncates
findings.failure_mode: a valid 32-bit metric value silently wraps into an incorrect u16, producing wrong data without any error signal
findings.fix: Use u16::try_from(parsed_u32) and propagate Allocation/Parse error on overflow

findings.problem: parts[0] and parts[1] unchecked indexing into a Vec produced by split(',') — empty lines or lines with fewer than 2 commas panic
findings.failure_mode: a single empty line or trailing newline in the file causes a bounds panic
findings.fix: Skip empty lines with .filter(|l| !l.trim().is_empty()), then use line.split_once(',') or check parts.len() >= 2 with .get(0)/.get(1) before indexing

findings.problem: println!() call inside load_metrics: logging is a hidden side effect embedded in a data-loading function
findings.failure_mode: side effects in a function that purports to load structured data break purity expectations, make the function untestable in isolation, and produce unwanted console output in library consumers
findings.fix: Remove println! entirely; if metrics/logging are needed, pass a callback or return a debug metadata field separate from the core data, or move all logging to the imperative shell layer

findings.problem: Record uses public String and u16 fields with no domain invariants — name can be empty, value can be zero with no semantic meaning
findings.failure_mode: callers can construct semantically invalid Records (e.g. name="", value=0 for a counter that should be >0) without compiler enforcement
findings.fix: Make fields private, add a Record::new(name: NonEmptyString, value: MetricValue) constructor that enforces invariants, and use newtype wrappers for domain-constrained types

findings.problem: collecting all split parts into Vec<String> with per-part .to_string() allocates a heap vector and clones every field — unnecessary for a simple two-field record
findings.failure_mode: increased allocation pressure and memory usage on each line; the intermediate Vec is discarded after one iteration
findings.fix: Use line.split_once(',') to get (&str, &str) in one shot, then trim and clone only the two needed values; avoid Vec allocation entirely

findings.problem: load_metrics returns Vec<Record> with no error type — all failures (I/O, parse, index) are silently converted to panics via unwrap()
findings.failure_mode: the caller has no way to distinguish between file-not-found, malformed data, and type-conversion errors; all manifest as runtime panics
findings.fix: Define a MetricError enum (Io, Parse, Truncation) and change the return type to Result<Vec<Record>, MetricError>
